title: Lemony chickpea skillet
description: Golden chickpeas, soft tomatoes, and a bright squeeze of lemon.
steps: Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Wash the tomatoes, spinach, and lemon. Halve the tomatoes.
Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the tomatoes and cook for 4–5 minutes until softened.
Add the chickpeas and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until hot throughout.
Fold in the spinach and cook for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Turn off the heat, squeeze over half the lemon, and divide between two bowls.
why: Gives your use-soon spinach and tomatoes the starring roles, with canned chickpeas for a quick meal.

title: A very green rice bowl
description: Warm rice, wilted greens, and chickpeas with lemon.
steps: Cook the rice with water according to its package directions. Choose a rice that cooks within 25 minutes for this recipe.
Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Wash the spinach and lemon.
Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in the chickpeas and cook for 3–4 minutes until hot throughout.
Add the spinach and stir for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Divide the cooked rice between bowls, top with the chickpeas and greens, then squeeze over lemon.
why: Uses the spinach you marked to use soon, with staples you already have. Check the rice package for its cooking time.

title: Tomato & chickpea salad
description: A bright, simple bowl for a day when the stove can wait.
steps: Rinse and drain the canned chickpeas. Wash and dry the tomatoes, spinach, and lemon.
Halve the tomatoes and roughly chop the spinach. Place in a bowl with the chickpeas.
Squeeze half the lemon into a small cup and whisk with the olive oil. Remove any lemon seeds.
Toss the dressing through the salad and divide between two bowls. Serve straight away.
why: A no-cook way to use your spinach and tomatoes. Canned chickpeas are ready to eat after draining and rinsing.
